submitted.rationale: Index 30 (Ni 0.17 / Sb 0.83) gave EQE 2.76%, far above the other two measured points. In its XRD, NiSb2O6 trirutile is joined by extra reflections that look like an Sb-oxide secondary phase. MACE puts Sb2O3 on the hull, which makes that secondary phase plausible.

rejected.reason: Close to the NiSb2O6 trirutile stoichiometry, but measured EQE was only 0.0054%
Measured EQE was only 0.016%; the high-EQE region is narrow, right at the Sb-rich edge
Ni-rich; XRD is dominated by trirutile/NiO-like peaks and there is no reason to expect better photoanode activity; not measured

consultations.verdict: Support. According to MACE, NiSb2O6 trirutile is on the hull (E_hull = 0), and XRD at indices 21 and 15 best matches it. MEGNet's HSE gap of 0.04 eV is likely an artifact of the magnetic Ni2+ state, so I treat it as uninformative. Index 22 (Sb 0.688) is closest to the phase-pure trirutile stoichiometry, which makes it the first measurement.

Weak support and mostly exploratory. Index 22 (near trirutile) gave a very low EQE. The XRD pattern at index 30 has extra peaks, suggesting a secondary Sb-oxide phase. MEGNet gives Sb2O3 a 2.8 eV gap, right at the 2.7 eV illumination energy, which is marginal. MACE puts NiSb2O4 well above the hull (0.28 eV/atom), so it is unlikely to form. I am sampling the opposite end of the composition line from the one measured.

Support. MACE puts Sb2O3 on the hull, so the Sb-oxide secondary phase coexisting with NiSb2O6 at the Sb-rich end is plausible. That fits EQE jumping 500x between index 22 and index 30. I am measuring index 28 to check whether the maximum sits just inside the Sb-rich edge.
